record.original_question: For every finitary unification problem in a syntactic equational theory, can pruning or freezing rules be designed so that the derivation tree generated by syntactic unification rules becomes finite and yields a finite complete set of unifiers?

evidence.quote: How to compute finite and complete sets of unifiers for any finitary unification problem of a syntactic equational theory.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let E be a syntactic equational theory over a first-order term signature; that is, an equational theory for which every E-equality s =_E t admits a proof by an equational replacement at the root using an axiom of E followed by paramodulations strictly below the root. Assume further that E is finitary, meaning that for every E-unification problem Γ (a finite set of equations to be solved modulo E) there exists a finite complete set of E-unifiers, i.e. a finite set S of substitutions such that:
  (i) every σ ∈ S is an E-unifier of Γ (σ(s) =_E σ(t) for each equation s = t in Γ), and
  (ii) for every E-unifier τ of Γ there exists σ ∈ S and a substitution ρ with τ =_E ρ ∘ σ on the variables of Γ.

The standard syntactic mutation-based unification calculus for E (the system of transformation rules: Decomposition, Mutate-with-axiom, Variable elimination, etc.) produces, from Γ, a derivation tree whose leaves labelled by solved forms correspond to E-unifiers. In general this derivation tree may be infinite even when E is finitary.

Question: Can one design uniform additional control rules — of "pruning" type (discarding redundant branches that produce only unifiers subsumed elsewhere in the tree) and/or "freezing" type (temporarily blocking the application of mutation steps on certain subterms to prevent non-terminating expansions) — that, when added to the syntactic mutation calculus, guarantee for every finitary syntactic equational theory E and every E-unification problem Γ that the resulting derivation tree is finite and that its solved-form leaves form a finite complete set of E-unifiers for Γ?
artifact.status_search_result: Available literature on syntactic equational theories and mutation-based unification (Kirchner, Jouannaud, and successors) treats the computation of finite complete sets of unifiers for finitary syntactic theories as an outstanding methodological problem; no general pruning/freezing strategy guaranteeing finite derivation trees for all finitary syntactic theories was located in web search. Status appears open.

status_evidence.title: Unification (computer science) - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Unification modulo equational theories is in general undecidable; unification type properties are in general undecidable.
status_evidence.claim: No uniform method is known to ensure termination of syntactic unification procedures for all finitary syntactic theories.

status_evidence.title: Unification Algorithm - an overview | ScienceDirect Topics
status_evidence.snippet: For an equational theory (Σ,E), unification is finitary if for any E-unification problem there is always a finite complete set of unifiers.
status_evidence.claim: Finitary unification is defined as existence of a finite complete set of unifiers, but computing one uniformly is not guaranteed by mutation rules.
